title:
Republicans earned this humiliation.

Newsflash for the GOP: campaigning on no new wars and lower prices, then starting
title_en:
Republicans earned this humiliation.

Newsflash for the GOP: campaigning on no new wars and lower prices, then starting a major war and raising prices, isn’t a good political strategy.

Trump and the Republican Party were handed a generational opportunity in 2024. 

Groups such as MAHA voters and young men, along with growing support among Hispanic and Muslim voters, helped give them a coalition that could have reshaped American politics for a generation.

They squandered it in two years.

What happened tonight is the opposite of political rocket science.

The GOP invited everyone into its “big tent,” then betrayed the people who showed up. 

Broken promises on virtually everything except closing the border. 

What did they expect would happen?

They confused support for their promises with unconditional loyalty to their party. 

They acted like winning an election meant they no longer had to listen to the people who won it for them.

The biggest slap in the face was to MAGA itself. 

Their most loyal supporters were promised a government that would finally put them first. 

Republicans cannot campaign on changing everything, fail to deliver on the things people care about most, and then blame those people for being angry.

The handling of the Epstein files, the promises surrounding DOGE being abandoned, and the endless cycle of big announcements followed with zero change or action only compounded the issue.

You cannot build an entire movement around exposing corruption and demanding accountability, then act offended when your own supporters demand both from you.

What exactly were Republicans asking voters to reward tonight? 

At some point, “the Democrats are worse” stops being a campaign and starts being an admission that you have nothing else to offer.

The Republican Party took an extraordinary political opening and turned it into a case study in arrogance, complacency, and wasted potential.

But you could argue this is the best possible outcome for Republicans before 2028. 

They just received a brutal warning while they still have two years to change course.

If their response is to blame voters, attack critics, and insist everything is going perfectly, they deserve what comes next.

Life after Trump is approaching. 

Republicans have to decide whether they will return to the neocon politics their own voters rejected, remain trapped in defending everything Trump does, or build a party capable of keeping its promises.

Democrats, meanwhile, have just been handed the opportunity Republicans wasted. 

Their biggest mistake would be assuming tonight means voters have embraced every part of the Democratic agenda.

Voters punishing Republicans is not a blank check for Democrats. 

If Democrats spend the next two years indulging their own ideological factions, letting the DSA set the direction, and dismissing concerns about affordability and everyday life, they will make the exact same mistake.

Republicans thought anger at Democrats would spare them from having to deliver. 

Democrats should not be stupid enough to believe anger at Republicans will spare them either.

Neither party owns the people who vote for it. 

Earn their trust, keep your promises, or expect to lose it.

共和党人应受这样的羞辱。

共和党的快讯：在竞选中主张不发动新的战争和降低价格，然后发动一场大规模战争并提高价格，这并不是一个好的政治策略。

2024 年，特朗普和共和党获得了一个世代相传的机会。

MAHA 选民和年轻人等团体，以及西班牙裔和穆斯林选民日益增长的支持，帮助他们建立了一个联盟，该联盟可能重塑一代人的美国政治。

两年之内他们就把它浪费掉了。

今晚发生的事情与政治火箭科学相反。

共和党邀请所有人进入它的“大帐篷”，然后背叛了出现的人。

除了关闭边境之外，几乎所有事情都没有兑现承诺。

他们期望会发生什么？

他们混淆了对自己承诺的支持和对政党的无条件忠诚。

他们表现得好像赢得选举意味着他们不再需要听取为他们赢得选举的人的意见。

最大的一记耳光是打给MAGA自己的。

他们最忠实的支持者得到了一个最终将他们放在第一位的政府的承诺。

共和党人不能在竞选中力图改变一切，未能实现人们最关心的事情，然后指责这些人的愤怒。

爱泼斯坦文件的处理、围绕 DOGE 的承诺被放弃，以及随之而来的无休止的重大公告、零变化或行动，只会让问题变得更加复杂。

你不能围绕揭露腐败和要求问责来发起一场完整的运动，然后当你自己的支持者要求你同时要求你做到这两点时，你又表现得被冒犯了。

共和党人今晚到底要求选民奖励什么？

在某种程度上，“民主党更糟糕”不再是一场竞选活动，而是开始承认你没有其他可提供的。

共和党采取了非同寻常的政治开放，并将其变成了傲慢、自满和浪费潜力的案例研究。

但你可能会说，这是共和党在 2028 年之前可能出现的最佳结果。

他们刚刚收到残酷的警告，而他们还有两年的时间改变路线。

如果他们的反应是指责选民、攻击批评者并坚称一切进展顺利，那么他们就活该承受接下来的后果。

特朗普之后的生活即将到来。

共和党人必须决定是否要回到被自己的选民拒绝的新保守主义政治，还是继续为特朗普所做的一切辩护，还是建立一个能够信守承诺的政党。

与此同时，民主党人刚刚获得了共和党人浪费的机会。

他们最大的错误是假设今晚意味着选民已经接受了民主党议程的各个部分。

选民惩罚共和党并不是民主党的空白支票。

如果民主党人在接下来的两年里放纵自己的意识形态派别，让 DSA 设定方向，并忽视对负担能力和日常生活的担忧，他们就会犯同样的错误。

共和党人认为对民主党人的愤怒会让他们不必兑现承诺。

民主党人不应该愚蠢到相信对共和党人的愤怒也会让他们幸免。

任何一方都不拥有投票给它的人。

赢得他们的信任，信守承诺，否则就会失去信任。

title:
Forcing the internal dynamics to be linear is overly restrictive, IMHO.
It requires a very large dimension for the state
title_en:
Forcing the internal dynamics to be linear is overly restrictive, IMHO.
It requires a very large dimension for the state representation.
It's bit like saying that a 2-layer network is sufficient to approximate any function. It's trues, but impractical. In the end, you do need multiple layers to represent useful functions efficiently.
title_zh:
恕我直言，强制内部动态呈线性是过于严格的。
它需要非常大的维度来表示状态。
这有点像说 2 层网络足以近似任何函数。这是事实，但不切实际。最后，您确实需要多个层来有效地表示有用的函数。

title:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records ca
title_en:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records can ruin lives.

GenLayer aims to settle AI-agent disputes in minutes: one AI validator proposes a verdict, others check independently, and decisions can be appealed.

On 27 March 2023, Alison MacPherson paid via RingGo on Hunter Street in Kirkcaldy. She typed 9 for 8 and missed the Z. A penalty followed.

Her receipt matched the time and place. A tribunal sided with her. Fife Council appealed. On 8 January 2024, the Upper Tribunal overturned it and sent it back.

The judge accepted her good faith, but the payment covered another car.

The payment was real. The registration wasn't hers.

Lee Castleton faced worse in the film: Horizon falsely showed a £23,000 gap. Without a lawyer, he faced £321,000 in legal costs and bankruptcy.

AI can't rewrite laws or guarantee truth. Millions of agent deals need evidence checked and decisions open to challenge.

If an AI agent pays under the wrong ID, what matters more: the receipt, the intent or the rule?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

GenLayer 的目标是在几分钟内解决人工智能代理纠纷：一名人工智能验证者提出裁决，其他人独立检查，并且可以对决定提出上诉。

2023 年 3 月 27 日，Alison MacPherson 在柯科迪亨特街通过 RingGo 付款。她8投9中，但没有击中Z。随后受到了处罚。

她的收据与时间和地点相符。法庭支持她。法伊夫议会提出上诉。 2024 年 1 月 8 日，上级法庭推翻了该判决并将其发回。

法官接受了她的诚意，但付款涵盖了另一辆车。

付款是真实的。登记不是她的。

李·卡斯尔顿 (Lee Castleton) 在影片中面临着更糟糕的情况：地平线错误地显示了 23,000 英镑的差距。在没有律师的情况下，他面临 321,000 英镑的法律费用和破产。

人工智能无法重写法律或保证真相。数以百万计的代理交易需要检查证据，决策也需要接受质疑。

如果人工智能代理使用错误的 ID 付款，收据、意图还是规则哪个更重要？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

title:

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people t
title_en:
People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.

People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.
title_zh:
人们应该始终掌控未来。

OpenAI 反对这样一种观念，即人们被降级到做“人工智能系统认为对人类有意义的奖励”的事情是可以接受的。

人们不应该将对未来的控制权交给超级智能，而这一要求最终应该限制人工智能的进步。

author: @newsfromgoogle

summary_en: Google announced that its education updates, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and AI Search, will be turned off by default, allowing schools to enable them individually. This move aims to address growing concerns from educators regarding student data privacy and classroom control.
summary_zh: 谷歌针对教育界对AI工具的隐私与控制担忧，宣布旗下Gemini等AI功能在教育版中默认处于关闭状态。
full_text_zh: 谷歌表示，其教育更新为学校提供了“更多选择，而不是更少”； Gemini、Gemini Notebook 和搜索默认处于关闭状态，可以单独启用

title:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff
title_en:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff for streams, fliers, YT stuff, banners, logos, etc...  A few big ticket items, but lots of little projects.

It is hands down the most miserable, time wasting, and laborious processes I've ever experienced when it comes to dealing with contract work.  And I did contracts in heavy civil construction...

A few thousand pissed down the drain on referred artists that just ghosted me after taking deposits.

Thumbnail artists that think they know what is better on a thumbnail than I do, so they completely ignore directions and do their own thing...

Logos that are copy right infringements or such near copies of other work it's shameful.

1 in 5.  MAYBE.  That's how many acted like actual professionals, delivered work on time, did what was asked, and finished the work.  Almost all of those were corporate firms too, not individuals.

It's so bad I've mostly just avoided having to use the industry when ever possible.  But the next time a big project I need comes up I'm going to double book it.

I'll go the traditional route, and the AI route.  And that is what will decide how I spend my money, and more importantly my time, going forward.

The OP is right.  Artists aren't saving their own careers.  They are pushing people to other less shitty interactions, and have been for years.

The difference is, there was no other choice before.  There is now.
title_zh:
在过去 20 年里，我在各种业务中在“艺术家”上花费了超过 15,000 美元。

委托艺术作品、流媒体内容、传单、YT 内容、横幅、徽标等……一些大项目，但还有很多小项目。

这无疑是我在处理合同工作时经历过的最痛苦、最浪费时间、最费力的
full_text_en:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff for streams, fliers, YT stuff, banners, logos, etc...  A few big ticket items, but lots of little projects.

It is hands down the most miserable, time wasting, and laborious processes I've ever experienced when it comes to dealing with contract work.  And I did contracts in heavy civil construction...

A few thousand pissed down the drain on referred artists that just ghosted me after taking deposits.

Thumbnail artists that think they know what is better on a thumbnail than I do, so they completely ignore directions and do their own thing...

Logos that are copy right infringements or such near copies of other work it's shameful.

1 in 5.  MAYBE.  That's how many acted like actual professionals, delivered work on time, did what was asked, and finished the work.  Almost all of those were corporate firms too, not individuals.

It's so bad I've mostly just avoided having to use the industry when ever possible.  But the next time a big project I need comes up I'm going to double book it.

I'll go the traditional route, and the AI route.  And that is what will decide how I spend my money, and more importantly my time, going forward.

The OP is right.  Artists aren't saving their own careers.  They are pushing people to other less shitty interactions, and have been for years.

The difference is, there was no other choice before.  There is now.
full_text_zh:
在过去 20 年里，我在各种业务中在“艺术家”上花费了超过 15,000 美元。

委托艺术作品、流媒体内容、传单、YT 内容、横幅、徽标等……一些大项目，但还有很多小项目。

这无疑是我在处理合同工作时经历过的最痛苦、最浪费时间、最费力的过程。 我还做过重型土木建筑合同……

几千名被推荐的艺术家在接受存款后就消失了。

缩略图艺术家认为他们比我更知道缩略图上的什么，所以他们完全无视指示并做自己的事情......

侵犯版权或近似复制其他作品的徽标是可耻的。

五分之一。也许吧。 这就是有多少人表现得像真正的专业人士，按时交付工作，完成要求的工作并完成工作。 几乎所有这些都是公司公司，而不是个人。

这太糟糕了，我基本上只是尽可能避免使用这个行业。 但下次当我需要一个大项目时，我会双重预订。

我会走传统路线和人工智能路线。 这将决定我如何花我的钱，更重要的是我的时间。

OP是对的。 艺术家并不是在拯救自己的职业生涯。 他们正在推动人们进行其他不那么糟糕的互动，而且多年来一直如此。

不同的是，之前没有其他选择。 现在有了。

title:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesl
title_en:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesla’s Cortex 1 and Cortex 2 clusters at Giga Texas are already in production at well over 200 MW combined, with a stated target of ~400 MW of SI (Super Intelligence) training compute by the end of 2026.  That capacity is primarily for training vehicle autonomy/FSD and Optimus models, remember those? 
We are running an enormous fleet on FSD.  
The difference vs SpaceX/xAI is priority. xAI is a pure AI lab that needs massive generic training flops for frontier models (and can sell excess capacity to Anthropic and others). 
Tesla’s highest-value use of the same capital is our proprietary real-world data flywheel for cars and bots. 
Diverting significant capacity to external customers would slow the exact products that justify Tesla’s valuation premium today.  

2. Merchant GPU compute is a brutal business Tesla doesn’t need to enter Rapid GPU depreciation and stranded capacity risk are real (Elon has commented on half-built data centers and idle chips). 
Nvidia owns the silicon stack; hyperscalers and specialized neoclouds already dominate the rental market. 

Tesla’s actual competitive advantage in the AI infrastructure stack is energy, not training chips. It has already sold hundreds of millions to ~$1B of Megapacks into the Colossus buildouts. That’s higher-margin, more defensible, and leverages what Tesla already does at scale.⁠ 
Selling raw flops would put Tesla in direct competition with Nvidia, AWS, CoreWeave, etc., in a capital-intensive, fast-depreciating business where it has no structural edge.  

3. The Dojo experience is a cautionary tale Tesla shut down Dojo in 2025 after Elon called the Dojo 2 design an “evolutionary dead end” and much of the team left. The company pivoted hard to Nvidia for training clusters while focusing its own silicon (AI5/AI6 and later) on inference in vehicles and robots. Re-entering custom training hardware at scale just to become a merchant seller would repeat a hard lesson.⁠ 

However, all this chip know-how is not lost and used now in the Terafab pilot.  

4. SpaceX’s speed is real, but it’s solving a different problem Colossus 1  and 2 are impressive, and SpaceX’s construction/execution culture is a genuine advantage for pure data-center buildouts. 

Tesla’s construction teams are optimized for vehicle and energy product factories, not multi-gigawatt pure-play AI campuses. 

SpaceX/xAI also benefits from being able to treat excess capacity as a revenue stream; Tesla’s equivalent excess capacity is better used accelerating FSD and Optimus software.⁠  

5. On “build it and sell it to SpaceX” Tesla is already the power supplier to those clusters. 
The more logical path (if any) is modular hardware like the Megapod rather than competing head-on as a pure compute seller. Even then, SpaceX is currently the world’s fastest large-scale data-center builder. 

Tesla’s scarce capital and engineering bandwidth is better spent on the products only Tesla can ship  

So, to sum it up:  
Tesla is already scaling to 400 MW of training compute for its own FSD and Optimus needs. 
Merchant GPU rental is a low-moat, high-depreciation business that Nvidia and the hyperscalers already own. 
Tesla’s real AI infrastructure edge is energy and the proprietary physical-world data only its fleet generates. 
Selling flops to SpaceX or anyone else would just slow the higher-value autonomy and robotics timeline.

full_text_zh:
这会比平常长一点：

1.特斯拉正在构建计算，只是为了我们自己的最高投资回报率用例特斯拉位于德克萨斯州 Giga 的 Cortex 1 和 Cortex 2 集群已经投入生产，总功率远超 200 MW，其既定目标是到 2026 年底实现约 400 MW 的 SI（超级智能）训练计算。该能力主要用于训练车辆自动驾驶/FSD 和 Optimus 模型，还记得那些吗？
我们在 FSD 上运行着一支庞大的车队。
与 SpaceX/xAI 的区别在于优先级。 xAI 是一个纯粹的人工智能实验室，需要针对前沿模型进行大量通用训练失败（并且可以将多余的产能出售给 Anthropic 和其他公司）。
特斯拉对同一资本的最高价值用途是我们用于汽车和机器人的专有现实世界数据飞轮。
将大量产能转移给外部客户将会减缓产品的生产速度，而这些产品恰恰证明了特斯拉目前的估值溢价是合理的。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。

title:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either
title_en:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either online or in Marfa, and everyone who collected a print. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Over the years, this space has become smaller and smaller, both on the artist and collector sides. It's been a journey of experimentation, evolution and constant adaptation to the market. Many people have left, while a much smaller group has continued to believe in this space and what we're building.

We've moved through NFTs, digital art, physical art and everything in between. And now, I feel like we're left with a small group of passionate artists, collectors and individuals who genuinely enjoy being here, regardless of where the market is going.

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙

full_text_zh:
谢谢你+一些未经过滤的想法。

首先，我想感谢所有花时间在网上或马尔法观看我的电影的人，以及所有收集印刷品的人。这对我来说确实意义重大。

多年来，无论是对于艺术家还是收藏家来说，这个空间都变得越来越小。这是一个实验、进化和不断适应市场的旅程。许多人已经离开，而一小部分人仍然相信这个领域和我们正在建设的东西。

我们已经经历了 NFT、数字艺术、实体艺术以及介于两者之间的一切。现在，我觉得我们留下了一小群充满热情的艺术家、收藏家和个人，他们真正喜欢在这里，无论市场走向何方。

作为一名风光摄影师，我经历过不少的高潮和低谷。我们都知道摄影与 NFT 和数字艺术空间有着复杂的关系，许多人质疑它的价值、它在艺术世界中的地位，或者干脆与媒体没有联系。

我很幸运成为 2021 年 SuperRare 的第一批摄影师之一，从那以后我的生活就不再一样了。

我有机会参与一些令人难以置信的项目，比如 FreeHawaiiPhoto，我在其中引入了 CC0 的想法，后来看到许多艺术家和主要的 NFT 项目都接受了它。我很早就有机会在 2021 年尝试人工智能，并最终完成了一项委托，将我带到了中国，这要感谢一位相信我愿景的收藏家。

我对我的旅程以及我为这个领域做出的贡献感到非常自豪。我并不总是完美的，今天我肯定会做一些不同的事情，但我一直试图为艺术家，尤其是摄影师辩护。

2023年，我用了整整一年的时间来写作和创作一本根据真实故事改编的儿童读物。我将其作为实体书和 NFT 相结合的高端限量版发布。不幸的是，它没有取得我所希望的成功。最近，我把剩下的书全部收起来，入库。奇怪的是，我并没有感到悲伤。我感到一种巨大的自豪感。

为遵循自己深信不疑的想法而感到自豪，即使它没有像我希望的那样引起那么多人的共鸣。为创造了一些美丽、有意义且与我以前所做的完全不同的东西而感到自豪。当然，有些事情本来可以做得更好，但我真诚地相信我创造了一个美丽而鼓舞人心的故事，子孙后代将会欣赏。

它提醒我追求你真正热爱的事情是多么重要，即使人们不理解它，即使结果不是你所期望的。

三年后，我来到了马尔法，在大约一百人面前展示了我的第一部短片纪录片。

尽管我们的空间变得越来越小，但我确实感受到了这个小社区的温暖、善良和同情心。

我的电影与 NFT 或生成艺术无关。这是关于山脉、身体耐力、个人成长以及我与摄影的关系。然而，人们还是出现了。他们观看、聆听、提出问题，其中一些人与作品的联系足以收集实物印刷品。

这对我来说意义重大，超出了我所能正确表达的范围。

我将生命的过去十年奉献给了摄影和山脉。这团火在某些时刻比其他时刻燃烧得更猛烈，但它从未停止增长。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我感觉自己与今天所创造的东西的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

玛法对我来说非常特别。我已经很久没有感受到这样的支持和赞赏了。它还提醒我，真正的人际关系、对话和分享的经历永远比社交媒体上的点赞或数字更有意义。

我非常感谢那些认识到我内心的火焰并继续以任何方式表示支持的人们。

2026 年成为一名独立艺术家很困难。我不会假装不是这样。

在这里，努力工作并不总是能转化为成功。你必须不断地挑战自己、适应、更加直言不讳、更加自信、更加引人注目，等等。创作艺术本身只是靠艺术谋生的一小部分。

我知道这并不是艺术家独有的。这是几乎所有企业经营的现实。拥有一款出色的产品，或者创造出令您深感自豪的东西，仅靠其本身是远远不够的。

但经历了所有的起起落落，经历了成功和失败的实验，这个社区迄今为止仍然是我所拥有过的最积极参与和支持的社区之一。

我不知道这个空间到底会走向何方，也不知道几年后它会是什么样子。但我知道，我一生中一些最有意义的机会、经历和人际关系都来自于其中。

为此，我将永远心怀感激。

我想我想说的是，成功并不总是像我们想象的那样。有时它是一个售罄的版本，有时它是一个几乎卖不出去的项目，有时它是一个房间里挤满了真正关心你倾注心血的人。

我正在学着欣赏这一切。

如果您已经读到这里，感谢您的阅读、来到这里并继续支持我的创作。这意味着比你知道的更多。 💙

title_en:
🚨 XENOBLADE CHRONICLES 2 is being recompiled for PC — and the opening sections are reportedly PLAYABLE! ⚔️🔥

Developer AksharDP has released an experimental Windows recompilation of Nintendo's Switch RPG, built on technology from XCX Recomp and TotK Recomp!

🔥 CURRENT PROGRESS:

✅ Game boots successfully and reaches the main menu!

✅ New Game works, with the opening cutscenes reportedly running!

✅ First battle playable, with working combat controls!

✅ Goldmouth reached, with functioning audio, dialogue and text!

✅ Vulkan 1.3 rendering and native PC input support!

✅ Windows installer available — no need to compile the project manually!

📦 Version 0.1.2 available now!

⚠️ VERY EARLY DEVELOPMENT!

The developer reports that the opening sections are working, but the full game is NOT confirmed playable. Expect graphical issues, crashes and incomplete functionality.

🧪 Independent gameplay verification is still needed.

⚙️ Built using static recompilation technology rather than conventional Switch emulation.

💿 Requires your own Xenoblade Chronicles 2 game files with update 3.0.1.

🛠️ Developed by AksharDP, with extensive assistance from Claude Code. The developer explicitly acknowledges that most of the code and documentation was AI-generated.

⭐ Star the GitHub repository to follow development!

🔗https://t.co/7BjMlecm5T

🌐 Discover more PC ports, recompilations and fan projects:

🔗https://t.co/9gMW2oj2lk

#XenobladeChronicles2 #Recompilation #PCGaming

✅ 新游戏正常运行，据报道正在播放开场过场动画！

✅ Vulkan 1.3 渲染和原生 PC 输入支持！

✅ 可用 Windows 安装程序 — 无需手动编译项目！

title_en:
We co-led @traversal_ai's $120M Series B at a $1B valuation.

AI will write most of our software. Keeping it running in production is the harder problem. @_anish_agarwal, Raj, Raaz, and Ahmed built an AI SRE that understands how production systems fit together. It finds what's broken, fixes it, and increasingly prevents it.

Nubank, Harvey, PepsiCo, Amex, and Blackstone are customers. ARR is up 9x this year and usage is up 100x.

我们共同领导了 @traversal_ai 的 1.2 亿美元 B 轮融资，估值为 10 亿美元。

人工智能将编写我们的大部分软件。让它在生产中保持运行是更困难的问题。 @_anish_agarwal、Raj、Raaz 和 Ahmed 构建了一个 AI SRE，它了解生产系统如何组合在一起。它发现损坏的地方，修复它，并越来越多地预防它。

Nubank、Harvey、百事可乐、美国运通和 Blackstone 都是客户。今年 ARR 增长了 9 倍，使用量增长了 100 倍。

很高兴能够支持团队关闭 AI 原生 SDLC 的外循环。

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!

It changed 0.0085% of them and with no training, it now reads this 1881 page instead of writing 16,399 characters of dots!

Prompt was basically: "read this, find a smallish OCR model and fix its repetition doom loops. You can spend up to 5 hours and $100 on @huggingface Jobs."

It only took under 3 hours in the end and about $10 of Jobs compute.

title: this is f*cking insane. you have been googling other people's thinking for 20 years, karpathy's one 5 minute setup gives
title_en:
this is f*cking insane. you have been googling other people's thinking for 20 years, karpathy's one 5 minute setup gives you a google that only searches your own, and you have never once installed it

andrej karpathy pulled 16M views on one idea: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain

every article you read, every podcast you heard, every meeting you took, every dm thread you had, every tweet you drafted, all of it searchable in one line forever

the people running it today do not open chatgpt anymore. they open their own search bar. and their search bar has 11 years of their own thinking in it

the stack:

→ brew install obsidian, mkdir ~/vault, cd ~/vault

→ open claude code in that folder, type "init CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"

→ drop any file into /raw (transcript, pdf, screenshot, meeting notes). type one word: ingest

→ claude writes a wiki page, links it to 5 existing ones, updates CLAUDE.md with any new pattern it caught about how you think

→ never open a blank chat again. every question goes through the vault. every answer cites your own sources with dates and links

5 minutes to wire. runs forever on the laptop already in front of you

the alpha most people miss:

> search your own vault in one line and the answer cites 5 of your own past notes with dates. google cites strangers. your vault cites you

> every ingest adds cross-links to 5 past pages automatically. after 90 days your vault answers questions you forgot you had

> CLAUDE.md learns how you argue, what you change your mind on, what you avoid saying. after month 3 it drafts posts in your voice better than you can at 2am

title:
BREAKING: I asked Claude Code to turn my WiFi router into a radar. It worked.

No camera. No extra sensor. Claude wrote
title_en:
BREAKING: I asked Claude Code to turn my WiFi router into a radar. It worked.

No camera. No extra sensor. Claude wrote the code in 40 minutes. It reads how the WiFi signal bends around bodies and draws them as moving shapes on a map of my apartment.

I ran it at night to test it. Living room: me. Kitchen: empty. Bedroom: a second shape.

I live alone.

I thought it was a bug. I walked to the bedroom. The shape didn’t move. The map showed it standing next to the bed, facing the door.

I turned it off. I still don’t know what the code was reading.

If your router is on right now, it’s already doing half the job.

full_text_en:
BREAKING: I asked Claude Code to turn my WiFi router into a radar. It worked.

No camera. No extra sensor. Claude wrote the code in 40 minutes. It reads how the WiFi signal bends around bodies and draws them as moving shapes on a map of my apartment.

I ran it at night to test it. Living room: me. Kitchen: empty. Bedroom: a second shape.

I live alone.

I thought it was a bug. I walked to the bedroom. The shape didn’t move. The map showed it standing next to the bed, facing the door.

I turned it off. I still don’t know what the code was reading.

If your router is on right now, it’s already doing half the job.

title:
Great way to think of your next AI use case ⬇️

You ended your work day and you still have items on your to-do list.

Re
title_en:
Great way to think of your next AI use case ⬇️

You ended your work day and you still have items on your to-do list.

Read that list. 

Those are the the problems that AI is still not good enough to solve for, we can't or don't trust it enough to solve for, or may never be good enough to solve for.

"I have to review this email before I send it" - consider that you don't trust AI enough to reason on that issue or it still doesn't quite write like you. Perhaps spend more time on your "write like me" skill or build out another eval for that process to catch the most common or obvious things you're reviewing for. 

"I have to fill this thing out online and it has to be perfect" - then computer use isn't good enough, or you don't know it's good enough. If it makes sense, ask AI to complete the task one-by-one, watch it work, witness its performance. What, if anything, failed? Can you improve it for next time?

"I have to wait for Bobby to respond to my email" - consider additional workflows supporting on team alignment or team handoffs, something that nearly every enterprise I speak with is still struggling with.

Literally just end your work day and look at what is still left. 

That list will tell you what of your own workflows to improve with AI or where you can carve out a business for others with the same lingering list item.

您结束了一天的工作，但待办事项清单上仍有项目。

阅读该列表。

这些是人工智能仍然不足以解决的问题，我们不能或不相信它能够解决，或者可能永远不足以解决。

“在发送之前我必须先检查一下这封电子邮件”——考虑到你对人工智能的信任度不够，无法在这个问题上进行推理，或者它的写作方式仍然不太像你。也许花更多的时间在你的“像我一样写作”技能上，或者为这个过程建立另一个评估，以捕捉你正在审查的最常见或最明显的事情。

“我必须在网上填写这个东西，而且它必须是完美的”——那么计算机的使用就不够好，或者你不知道它足够好。如果有意义，请人工智能一项一项地完成任务，观察它的工作，见证它的表现。如果有什么失败的话？下次可以改进一下吗？

“我必须等待 Bobby 回复我的电子邮件”——考虑支持团队协调或团队交接的额外工作流程，这是我接触过的几乎每个企业仍在努力解决的问题。

从字面上看，只是结束一天的工作，看看还剩下什么。

title:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year
title_en:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year:
- 20,000 paying customers
- 252 million visitors
- 2.4 billion requests
- 2.4 petabyte (PB) in bandwidth

(~$8,000/mo if you add the $7,000/mo GPU bill and $800/mo R2 storage I pay for Photo AI, I exclude it above because it's one project that's so much more expensive in size than all the other sites together, but included in the chart below)

Claude Code helped me to find smart ways to save more money, AI is just really really really good at finding cost savings by itself, which is not so great for the economy short-term, but long term it trims all the fat and opens up spending for better investments I think

Anyway here's what it saved me in money, almost $34,000/mo:

- $29,000/mo - switched to better and cheaper video models on Photo AI, video was very expensive and since I didn't update it ever it stayed expensive, also routed some image jobs to Google Cloud where I have some Google Cloud Credits, and also routed some jobs to Sume which sells AI models at market cost, very cool! This made my GPU bill go from $36,000/mo to $7,000/mo

- $3,000/mo - consolidated my servers, cancelled Digital Ocean and Linode and moved everything to Hetzner saving about $3,000/mo

- $1100/mo - analyzed my Backblaze B2 server backups, I had infinite versioning and lifecycle policies, that's reduced now to 30 days, this literally pushed the bill from $1,200/mo to $26/mo, about 50x cheaper! I had essentially versions of files for all my servers for over a decade, crazy!

- $400/mo - similarly added Lifecycle Policies to my Cloudflare R2 bucket for Photo AI, pics are automatically put in cheaper Infrequent Access after 90 days, there was years of photos in there so this reduced the R2 bill from $1,200/mo to $800/mo

- $118/mo - Claude analyzed all my Cloudflare Domain registrations, lots of domains I didn't use and didn't make sense to keep paying for, lots of things that also don't really make sense anymore in a post-AGI world, renewals for .io TLD are now $50/year which adds up fast!

- $100/mo - Claude also analyzed my Claude subscription (yes!) and discovered I don't even use the Max 20x plan limits, so I downgraded from $200/mo to $100/mo

Even including Photo AI, I have now cut my costs by 90% from last year, getting me close to my biz expenses amount from a decade ago when I started building things

Costs slowly creep up over the years and you don't realize all the things you're spending on but AI is nice to help you figure all that out (also in your personal life!)

full_text_zh:
💸 更新：我的总商务费用现已降至每月约 300 美元！

这是为了运行我每年提供服务的所有网站/应用程序：
- 20,000 名付费客户
- 2.52 亿游客
- 24 亿个请求
- 2.4 PB 带宽

（如果加上我为 Photo AI 支付的 7,000 美元/月 GPU 费用和 800 美元/月 R2 存储费用，大约为 8,000 美元/月，我在上面排除了它，因为它是一个项目，其规模比所有其他网站加起来要贵得多，但包含在下面的图表中）

Claude Code 帮助我找到了节省更多钱的明智方法，人工智能本身真的非常非常擅长节省成本，这对短期经济来说并不是那么好，但从长远来看，它会削减所有的脂肪并为更好的投资打开支出

不管怎样，这就是它为我节省的钱，大约 34,000 美元/月：

- 29,000 美元/月 - 在 Photo AI 上切换到更好、更便宜的视频模型，视频非常昂贵，因为我没有更新它，所以它仍然很昂贵，还将一些图像作业路由到 Google Cloud，在那里我有一些 Google Cloud Credits，并且还将一些作业路由到 Sume，它以市场成本销售 AI 模型，非常酷！这使得我的 GPU 账单从 36,000 美元/月增加到 7,000 美元/月

- 每月 3,000 美元 - 整合了我的服务器，取消了 Digital Ocean 和 Linode，并将所有内容转移到 Hetzner，每月节省了约 3,000 美元

- 1100 美元/月 - 分析了我的 Backblaze B2 服务器备份，我有无限的版本控制和生命周期策略，现在减少到 30 天，这实际上将账单从 1,200 美元/月推至 26 美元/月，便宜了大约 50 倍！十多年来，我的所有服务器基本上都有文件版本，太疯狂了！

- 400 美元/月 - 同样在我的 Cloudflare R2 存储桶中添加用于照片 AI 的生命周期策略，90 天后图片会自动放入更便宜的不频繁访问中，那里有多年的照片，因此这将 R2 费用从 1,200 美元/月减少到 800 美元/月

- 118 美元/月 - Claude 分析了我所有的 Cloudflare 域名注册，很多域名我没有使用过，也没有必要继续付费，很多东西在后 AGI 世界中也不再有意义，.io TLD 的续订现在是 50 美元/年，加起来很快！

- 100 美元/月 - Claude 还分析了我的 Claude 订阅（是的！），发现我什至没有使用 Max 20x 计划限制，因此我从 200 美元/月降级至 100 美元/月

即使包括 Photo AI，我现在也比去年削减了 90% 的成本，这让我接近十年前开始构建产品时的业务支出金额

多年来，成本慢慢上升，你并没有意识到你花在了所有的事情上，但人工智能可以很好地帮助你弄清楚所有这些（也在你的个人生活中！）

title:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was
title_en:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was speaking to a relatively tech-forward operator at a distributor. Smart team, AI licenses for everyone, two or three people sharp enough to start building.

“We’ve built some great stuff. I just wouldn’t put any of it in front of a customer.”

His team has the same thing in common with almost every PE portco I talk to.

They have a pile of agents:

→ A pricing tool someone built in Claude Code.
→ A folder of “skills”.
→ A prototype vibe coded by a contractor.
→ A daily briefing assistant for the CEO.

They have budget and a sponsor too. Most of them even have urgency.

But every agent still lives on the laptop of whoever built it.

That's the pattern in every case: leadership treats agents as something the builder should maintain “on the side.”

An EA runs the CEO’s calendar and also babysits five bots.

This operator runs finance & ops and “owns” the pricing tool he built in Claude Code.

A contractor vibe codes a prototype, and nobody can say what it would take to keep it running once his contract ends.

I asked one PE partner how many of his portfolio companies have an agent hosted somewhere real. "One, maybe."

A laptop isn’t production, and "on the side" isn’t ownership.

You either give the agent a home (hosted, with an owner, access controls, monitoring, and a spend cap), turn it into a script, or kill it.

Most leadership teams just leave it on a laptop and call it a pilot.
title_zh:
现在，每家严肃的私募股权投资公司都拥有人工智能代理。

除了在某人的笔记本电脑上运行之外，很少有人在任何地方运行。

我正在与一家分销商的一位技术相对先进的操作员交谈。聪明的团队，每个人都有人工智能许可证，两三个人足够敏锐就可以开始构建。
full_text_en:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was speaking to a relatively tech-forward operator at a distributor. Smart team, AI licenses for everyone, two or three people sharp enough to start building.

“We’ve built some great stuff. I just wouldn’t put any of it in front of a customer.”

His team has the same thing in common with almost every PE portco I talk to.

They have a pile of agents:

→ A pricing tool someone built in Claude Code.
→ A folder of “skills”.
→ A prototype vibe coded by a contractor.
→ A daily briefing assistant for the CEO.

They have budget and a sponsor too. Most of them even have urgency.

But every agent still lives on the laptop of whoever built it.

That's the pattern in every case: leadership treats agents as something the builder should maintain “on the side.”

An EA runs the CEO’s calendar and also babysits five bots.

This operator runs finance & ops and “owns” the pricing tool he built in Claude Code.

A contractor vibe codes a prototype, and nobody can say what it would take to keep it running once his contract ends.

I asked one PE partner how many of his portfolio companies have an agent hosted somewhere real. "One, maybe."

A laptop isn’t production, and "on the side" isn’t ownership.

You either give the agent a home (hosted, with an owner, access controls, monitoring, and a spend cap), turn it into a script, or kill it.

Most leadership teams just leave it on a laptop and call it a pilot.
full_text_zh:
现在，每家严肃的私募股权投资公司都拥有人工智能代理。

除了在某人的笔记本电脑上运行之外，很少有人在任何地方运行。

我正在与一家分销商的一位技术相对先进的操作员交谈。聪明的团队，每个人都有人工智能许可证，两三个人足够敏锐就可以开始构建。

“我们已经构建了一些很棒的东西。我只是不会把它们放在客户面前。”

他的团队与我交谈过的几乎所有 PE Portco 都有相同的共同点。

他们有一堆代理：

→ 有人用 Claude Code 构建的定价工具。
→ “技能”文件夹。
→ 由承包商编码的原型氛围。
→ 首席执行官的每日简报助理。

他们也有预算和赞助商。他们中的大多数人甚至都有紧迫感。

但每个特工仍然依赖于建造它的人的笔记本电脑。

这就是每种情况下的模式：领导层将代理视为建筑商应该“站在一边”维护的东西。

EA 负责管理 CEO 的日历，并照顾五个机器人。

该运营商负责财务和运营，并“拥有”他在 Claude Code 中构建的定价工具。

承包商氛围对原型进行了编码，没有人能说出在合同结束后如何才能使其保持运行。

我问一位私募股权合伙人，他的投资组合公司中有多少家在真实的地方设有代理人。 “一个，也许吧。”

笔记本电脑不是生产产品，“二手”也不是所有权。

您要么给代理一个家（托管，有所有者、访问控制、监控和支出上限），要么将其变成脚本，要么杀死它。

大多数领导团队只是将其放在笔记本电脑上并称之为试点。

title_en:
I made an AI agent plan a $3,600 Greece trip for two.

Then asked it to plan another trip to Portugal.

Guess how much of the workflow I had to rebuild?

ZERO.

I used Teamily AI's team agents to handle the research and destination comparisons while my teammate and I reviewed the options.

It reminded me of this line from Summer's piece:

"Humans + Agents. One Team."

Here's what I did:

→ Created a Travel Research Agent
→ Built a Loop with the agent, me, and my teammate
→ Asked it to research a 5-day Greece trip and rank the best options
→ Reviewed the shortlist together in the group

Then reused the SAME Loop for Portugal.

All I had to do was change the trip requirements and run it again.

No repeating instructions or setting up everyone's roles twice.

I'd much rather have the agent do the research and leave the actual decisions to us.

title: Following the conclusion of two days of Government-to-Government negotiations today in Kampala , Germany has committed €
title_en:
Following the conclusion of two days of Government-to-Government negotiations today in Kampala , Germany has committed €50 million in grants to Uganda to support development interventions in water, electricity, agribusiness, local economic development and refugee-hosting communities

The commitment comprises €30 million in Financial Cooperation and €20 million in Technical Cooperation, reinforcing a bilateral partnership spanning more than 60 years.

Of the new support, €35 million (70%) will go towards water and electricity, while €10 million (20%) will support agribusiness and local economies. The remaining €5 million will support refugee participation and host communities, among other areas.

I stated that the interventions are aligned with Uganda's National Development Plan IV and Tenfold Growth Strategy, which aims to grow the economy to US$500 billion by 2040 through Agro-Industrialisation, Tourism, Minerals, and Science, Technology and Innovation (ATMS).

We appreciate this support. It comes at a time when resources for overseas development support are under pressure across Europe given the on-going global challenges.

I welcomed the €35 million allocation to water and electricity, describing these as important enablers of the ATMS agenda. I also called on German investors to explore opportunities in production, processing, exports and skilled job creation, proposing structured engagements to identify bankable investment opportunities.

The negotiations also earmarked €18 million for the electrification of West Nile, which is expected to serve enterprises and farms in a region that trades with eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. 

I further asked Germany to support Uganda's efforts to mobilise financing for railway development, irrigation and electricity through the World Bank, African Development Bank and other multilateral institutions.

full_text_zh:
今天在坎帕拉结束为期两天的政府间谈判后，德国承诺向乌干达提供 5000 万欧元赠款，以支持水、电、农业综合企业、当地经济发展和难民收容社区的发展干预措施

该承诺包括 3000 万欧元的金融合作和 2000 万欧元的技术合作，以加强长达 60 多年的双边伙伴关系。

在新的支持中，3500万欧元（70%）将用于水和电力，1000万欧元（20%）将用于支持农业企业和当地经济。剩余的 500 万欧元将用于支持难民参与和收容社区等领域。

我表示，这些干预措施与乌干达的国家发展计划 IV 和十倍增长战略相一致，该战略的目标是通过农业工业化、旅游业、矿产以及科学、技术和创新 (ATMS)，到 2040 年将经济增长到 5000 亿美元。

我们感谢这种支持。鉴于当前的全球挑战，整个欧洲的海外发展支持资源都面临压力。

我对 3500 万欧元的水电拨款表示欢迎，并将其描述为 ATMS 议程的重要推动因素。我还呼吁德国投资者探索生产、加工、出口和创造熟练就业机会的机会，提出结构化的合作来确定可融资的投资机会。

谈判还指定了1800万欧元用于西尼罗河的电气化，预计将为与刚果民主共和国东部和南苏丹有贸易往来的地区的企业和农场提供服务。

我还请德国支持乌干达通过世界银行、非洲开发银行和其他多边机构为铁路发展、灌溉和电力筹集资金的努力。

title_en:
Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, but if you’re in a throwaway container and are okay with those running without asking, you can now set CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1.

And shell commands that hit their timeout now keep running in the background instead of getting cut off, so a long build or test suite isn’t killed halfway.

title:
GERMANY COMMITS €50M GRANT TO UGANDA FOR DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS

Germany has committed €50 million in grants to Uganda to
title_en:
GERMANY COMMITS €50M GRANT TO UGANDA FOR DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS

Germany has committed €50 million in grants to Uganda to support development interventions in water, electricity, agribusiness, local economic development and refugee-hosting communities, following the conclusion of two days of Government-to-Government negotiations in Kampala on November 3, 2026.

The commitment comprises €30 million in Financial Cooperation and €20 million in Technical Cooperation, reinforcing a bilateral partnership spanning more than 60 years.

Of the new support, €35 million (70%) will go towards water and electricity, while €10 million (20%) will support agribusiness and local economies. The remaining €5 million will support refugee participation and host communities, among other areas.

The Finance Minister @henrymusasizi1 said the interventions are aligned with Uganda's National Development Plan IV and Tenfold Growth Strategy, which aims to grow the economy to US$500 billion by 2040 through Agro-Industrialisation, Tourism, Minerals, and Science, Technology and Innovation (ATMS).

“We appreciate this support. It comes at a time when resources for overseas development support are under pressure across Europe given the on-going global challenges,” Musasizi said.

He welcomed the €35 million allocation to water and electricity, describing these as important enablers of the ATMS agenda. He also called on German investors to explore opportunities in production, processing, exports and skilled job creation, proposing structured engagements to identify bankable investment opportunities.

The negotiations also earmarked €18 million for the electrification of West Nile, which is expected to serve enterprises and farms in a region that trades with eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. 

Musasizi further asked Germany to support Uganda's efforts to mobilise financing for railway development, irrigation and electricity through the World Bank, African Development Bank and other multilateral institutions.

The Head of the German Delegation, Joachim Schmitt, who also heads the Central and East Africa Division at Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, said the cooperation would support Uganda's ambition to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status.

“Our development cooperation will actively support this strategy, while being fully aligned to the Ugandan Vision 2040, its '10-fold growth strategy', including the ATMS priorities, as well as the 'National Development Plan IV',” Schmitt said.

He emphasised increased participation of Ugandan, German and European enterprises in unlocking economic potential, creating jobs and supporting Uganda's development. He also commended Uganda's refugee-hosting policies, reaffirming Germany's continued focus on West Nile and support for refugees and host communities.

German Ambassador to Uganda, H.E. Sigrid Sommer, said the new commitments build on more than six decades of cooperation that have delivered tangible results. “With these additional bilateral commitments, Germany remains a strong partner of Uganda and its people.”

Sommer said the outcome of the negotiations provides a basis for development cooperation over the next two years, aligned with Uganda's strategies and priorities. 

She noted that Germany accounts for nearly 25% of EU funding and reaffirmed her country's commitment to supporting Uganda alongside partners, including GIZ and KfW.

She emphasised that development cooperation,trade and investment are complementary parts of the partnership, adding that Germany remains committed to presenting business opportunities to enhance trade and investment with Uganda.

full_text_zh:
德国承诺向乌干达提供 5000 万欧元赠款用于发展项目

2026 年 11 月 3 日在坎帕拉结束为期两天的政府间谈判后，德国承诺向乌干达提供 5000 万欧元赠款，支持水、电、农业综合企业、当地经济发展和难民收容社区的发展干预措施。

该承诺包括 3000 万欧元的金融合作和 2000 万欧元的技术合作，以加强长达 60 多年的双边伙伴关系。

在新的支持中，3500万欧元（70%）将用于水和电力，1000万欧元（20%）将用于支持农业企业和当地经济。剩余的 500 万欧元将用于支持难民参与和收容社区等领域。

财政部长 @henrymusasizi1 表示，这些干预措施符合乌干达国家发展计划 IV 和十倍增长战略，旨在通过农业工业化、旅游业、矿产以及科学、技术和创新 (ATMS) 到 2040 年将经济增长至 5000 亿美元。

穆萨西兹表示：“我们感谢这种支持。鉴于当前的全球挑战，整个欧洲的海外发展支持资源都面临压力。”

他对 3500 万欧元的水电拨款表示欢迎，并将其描述为 ATMS 议程的重要推动者。他还呼吁德国投资者探索生产、加工、出口和创造熟练就业岗位的机会，并提出结构化参与以确定可融资的投资机会。

谈判还指定了1800万欧元用于西尼罗河的电气化，预计将为与刚果民主共和国东部和南苏丹有贸易往来的地区的企业和农场提供服务。

穆萨西齐进一步要求德国支持乌干达通过世界银行、非洲开发银行和其他多边机构为铁路发展、灌溉和电力筹集资金的努力。

德国代表团团长、德国联邦经济合作与发展部中非和东非司司长约阿希姆·施密特表示，此次合作将支持乌干达摆脱最不发达国家地位的雄心。

施密特表示：“我们的发展合作将积极支持这一战略，同时完全符合乌干达2040年愿景、‘十倍增长战略’，包括ATMS优先事项以及‘国家发展计划IV’。”

他强调乌干达、德国和欧洲企业更多地参与释放经济潜力、创造就业机会和支持乌干达的发展。他还赞扬乌干达的难民收容政策，重申德国继续关注西尼罗河并支持难民和收容社区。

德国驻乌干达大使 H.E.西格丽德·索默 (Sigrid Sommer) 表示，新的承诺建立在六十多年的合作基础上，这些合作已经取得了切实成果。 “通过这些额外的双边承诺，德国仍然是乌干达及其人民的强有力的合作伙伴。”

索默表示，谈判结果为未来两年的发展合作奠定了基础，符合乌干达的战略和优先事项。

她指出，德国占欧盟资金的近 25%，并重申德国致力于与德国国际合作机构 (GIZ) 和德国复兴信贷银行 (KfW) 等合作伙伴一起支持乌干达。

她强调，发展合作、贸易和投资是伙伴关系的补充部分，并补充说，德国仍然致力于提供商业机会，以加强与乌干达的贸易和投资。

Why manage a different inference setup for every AI agent task?

Search, OCR, classification, extraction, reranking... it adds up.

Superlinked SIE brings 200+ open models behind one API.

It's open source (Apache 2.0), available as a hosted service, and can also be self-hosted when you need more control.

One inference layer. A lot less complexity.

title: DOE just dropped its Fall 2026 SBIR/STTR Phase 1 topics, with more than $200M in funding available to small businesses b
title_en:
DOE just dropped its Fall 2026 SBIR/STTR Phase 1 topics, with more than $200M in funding available to small businesses building in energy + national security. Here's a look at the 25 topics:

Topic 1: Advanced technologies for domestic critical mineral extraction, midstream processing, and recycling: small-market minerals like vanadium, hafnium, zirconium. Each proposal must pair a real feedstock provider with a processor

Topic 2: Innovations in manufacturing scale-up for energy applications: production bottlenecks, modular/retrofit platforms, smart manufacturing tools

Topic 3: State-of-the-art tech for industrial competitiveness: energy-intensive industries, cross-sector processes, data center and large load integration

Topic 4: Next-generation building technologies: dual-fuel HVAC, SI/ML controls

Topic 5: Cutting edge generation and power management technologies: hydro, marine, wind and PV recycling, solar thermal, space PV, interconnection, permitting

Topic 6: Advanced transportation and fuels production: fuels from alternative feedstocks, MW-scale fuel cells for data centers, heavy-rare-earth-free motors, off-road and mining powertrains

Topic 7: Battery technologies for dual-use applications: cell-level demos w/ commercial markets and defense uses like UAS, UUV, soldier-carried power

Topic 8: Advanced cybersecurity, resilience, and energy system risk mitigation technologies: OT/ICS security, supply chain assurance, recovery tools

Topic 9: Innovative technologies for hydrocarbons and geothermal energy: modernizing coal mines and plants, oil and gas recovery, produced water sensors, geothermal targeting and storage

Topic 10: Reactor concepts: HTGR/MSR components, liquid metal, sCO2, digital twins, construction cost reduction

Topic 11: Fuel cycle R&D: domestic fuel supply chain, TRISO and advanced fuels, used fuel recovery, materials accounting

Topic 12: Nuclear energy enabling tech: reactor sensors, advanced materials, modeling tools, post-irradiation exam

Topic 13: Advanced technologies for used nuclear fuel and high-level waste disposition: standardized waste packages, dry storage modeling, licensing pathways for DOE’s nuclear lifecycle campuses

Topic 14: Grid innovations to strengthen the electric system's capacity: grid cyber, grid-enhancing tech, microgrids, stationary storage, large load interconnection

Topic 15: Commercializing ASCR/ECP-funded HPC software 

Topic 16: Cybersecurity for scientific high-performance computing 

Topic 17: Novel instrumentation for X-ray and neutron facilities: permanent magnet accelerator elements, in-situ optics cleaning, neutron mirrors and detectors

Topic 18: Data, synthesis, and characterization strategies for SI-driven materials and molecular systems discovery: ML-guided membranes for critical mineral/REE separation, SI data platforms

Topic 19: Enabling technologies for bioengineering and quantum science-based sensors: field-deployable quantum sensing, quantum bioimaging, Super Intelligence for bioenergy crop engineering, big biological data

Topic 20: Fusion fuel cycle and enabling technologies: tritium handling, fueling, exhaust processing, detritiation

Topic 21: Advanced particle and radiation detectors: ultra-radiopure materials, high-rate detectors, vibration-free cryogenics

Topic 22: High-performance electronics and data acquisition systems 

Topic 23: Accelerator science and tech: superconducting magnets, RF power, sources and lasers, diagnostics

Topic 24: Proliferation detection: entangled-photon remote sensing, hyperspectral imagery over water to support monitoring of nuclear-powered ships, radiation detection, radiological source replacement

Topic 25: Nuclear detonation detection: field data acquisition, calibration tools, rad-hard microcircuits

Pitches due Dec. 16.

full_text_zh:
美国能源部刚刚放弃了 2026 年秋季 SBIR/STTR 第一阶段主题，为小型企业提供超过 2 亿美元的资金用于能源和国家安全建设。以下是这 25 个主题：

主题一：国内关键矿产开采、中游加工和回收的先进技术：钒、铪、锆等小市场矿产。每个提案必须将真正的原料供应商与加工商配对

主题2：能源应用制造规模化创新：生产瓶颈、模块化/改造平台、智能制造工具

主题三：最先进的产业竞争力技术：能源密集型产业、跨行业流程、数据中心和大负载集成

主题 4：下一代建筑技术：双燃料 HVAC、SI/ML 控制

主题 5：尖端发电和电力管理技术：水力、海洋、风能和光伏回收、太阳能热利用、太空光伏、互连、许可

主题 6：先进运输和燃料生产：替代原料燃料、数据中心用兆瓦级燃料电池、无重稀土电机、越野和采矿动力总成

主题 7：军民两用应用的电池技术：商业市场和国防用途（如 UAS、UUV、士兵携带电源）的电池级演示

主题 8：先进的网络安全、弹性和能源系统风险缓解技术：OT/ICS 安全、供应链保证、恢复工具

主题 9：碳氢化合物和地热能创新技术：煤矿和工厂现代化、石油和天然气回收、采出水传感器、地热定位和存储

主题 10：反应堆概念：HTGR/MSR 组件、液态金属、sCO2、数字孪生、降低建设成本

主题11：燃料循环研发：国内燃料供应链、TRISO和先进燃料、废燃料回收、物料核算

主题 12：核能使能技术：反应堆传​​感器、先进材料、建模工具、辐照后检查

主题 13：废旧核燃料和高放废物处置的先进技术：标准化废物包装、干式储存模型、能源部核生命周期园区的许可途径

主题 14：增强电力系统能力的电网创新：电网网络、电网增强技术、微电网、固定存储、大负载互连

主题 15：ASCR/ECP 资助的 HPC 软件商业化

主题 16：科学高性能计算的网络安全

主题 17：X 射线和中子设施的新型仪器：永磁加速器元件、原位光学清洁、中子镜和探测器

主题 18：SI 驱动材料和分子系统发现的数据、合成和表征策略：用于关键矿物/稀土元素分离的 ML 引导膜、SI 数据平台

主题19：生物工程和基于量子科学的传感器的使能技术：可现场部署的量子传感、量子生物成像、生物能源作物工程的超级智能、生物大数据

主题 20：聚变燃料循环和使能技术：氚处理、加燃料、废气处理、脱氚

主题 21：先进粒子和辐射探测器：超辐射纯材料、高速率探测器、无振动低温技术

主题 22：高性能电子和数据采集系统

主题 23：加速器科学与技术：超导磁体、射频功率、光源和激光器、诊断

主题 24：扩散探测：纠缠光子遥感、支持核动力船舶监测的水上高光谱图像、辐射探测、放射源替代

主题 25：核爆炸探测：现场数据采集、校准工具、抗辐射微电路

推介截止日期为 12 月 16 日。

title_en:
The holidays are fast approaching, so I’m back with my sixth (!!) annual gift guide. 

It's got over 100 gift ideas—all things I actually use, love, and recommend.

This started out as a random post idea, but now you’d be surprised how many people ping me asking when the new list will be out.

As always, the collection includes a mix of practical stuff with a lot of fun and delight, from high-end products to very affordable items. There are no affiliate links here, and I’m not benefiting from recommending any of these products.

Pro tip: After reading it, point your favorite AI agent at the post and have it brainstorm gifts for your family, friends, and coworkers.

Here's the guide: https://t.co/cTzHGwV4Bh
title_zh:

title:
1987 BR Chopra’s Mahabharat was far more realistic and authentic.

Characters felt grounded and human, dialogues carried
title_en:
1987 BR Chopra’s Mahabharat was far more realistic and authentic.

Characters felt grounded and human, dialogues carried real weight and depth, and the overall tone stayed closer to the epic’s gravity. War scenes (shot in real open locations), performances, and storytelling had a seriousness that still holds up decades later.

Star Plus version was also good and more polished in production, but the loud BGM, heavy reliance on VFX, and portrayal of Krishna as a consistently sweet, smiling, flute-playing guy made it feel more like a modern spectacle than the complex, strategic, and sometimes fierce Krishna of the text.

Especially the Virata War — BR Chopra showed it accurately: Arjuna single-handedly dominated the Kaurava army, and Karna was nowhere near his level. Star Plus version glorified Karna and had Bhishma stop the fight, turning it into unnecessary drama.

Both have their place, but the 1987 version still feels more like “Mahabharata.”
title_zh:
1987 年 BR Chopra 的《摩诃婆罗多》更加现实和真实。

角色给人一种脚踏实地、人性化的感觉，对话具有真正的分量和深度，整体基调更接近史诗的严肃性。战争场景（在真实的开放地点拍摄）、表演和讲故事的严肃性在几十年后仍然存在。

full_text_en:
1987 BR Chopra’s Mahabharat was far more realistic and authentic.

Characters felt grounded and human, dialogues carried real weight and depth, and the overall tone stayed closer to the epic’s gravity. War scenes (shot in real open locations), performances, and storytelling had a seriousness that still holds up decades later.

Star Plus version was also good and more polished in production, but the loud BGM, heavy reliance on VFX, and portrayal of Krishna as a consistently sweet, smiling, flute-playing guy made it feel more like a modern spectacle than the complex, strategic, and sometimes fierce Krishna of the text.

Especially the Virata War — BR Chopra showed it accurately: Arjuna single-handedly dominated the Kaurava army, and Karna was nowhere near his level. Star Plus version glorified Karna and had Bhishma stop the fight, turning it into unnecessary drama.

Both have their place, but the 1987 version still feels more like “Mahabharata.”
full_text_zh:
1987 年 BR Chopra 的《摩诃婆罗多》更加现实和真实。

角色给人一种脚踏实地、人性化的感觉，对话具有真正的分量和深度，整体基调更接近史诗的严肃性。战争场景（在真实的开放地点拍摄）、表演和讲故事的严肃性在几十年后仍然存在。

Star Plus 版本也很不错，在制作上也更加精致，但是响亮的 BGM、对视觉特效的严重依赖，以及将克里希纳描绘成一个一贯甜美、微笑、吹长笛的家伙，让它感觉更像是一个现代奇观，而不是文本中复杂、战略性、有时甚至是凶猛的克里希纳。

尤其是维拉塔战争——BR乔普拉准确地展示了这一点：阿朱那一手统治了考拉瓦军队，而卡纳远不及他的水平。 Star Plus版本荣耀了卡纳并让比什玛停止了战斗，将其变成了不必要的戏剧。

两者各有千秋，但 1987 年的版本仍然感觉更像《摩诃婆罗多》。

title: First of all, I want to make it absolutely clear that nothing I’m about to say changes the fact that SingChimon deserved
title_en:
First of all, I want to make it absolutely clear that nothing I’m about to say changes the fact that SingChimon deserved a main series of their own. They’ve more than proven that they have what it takes to carry one. That being said, as much as I would have loved to see them get that opportunity, I somehow find myself glad that things turned out the way they did.

Sing and Chimon will have a total of four GMMTV series that will most likely air next year. Three of them are already in production and the fourth is apparently about to start filming soon. That’s a lot of content to look forward to, but more importantly, it’s four projects that are actually moving forward.

Especially nowadays, I find it increasingly important to look beyond just getting a main series announced during a lineup presentation. Because what does an announcement ultimately mean if a project never makes it to production or gets postponed indefinitely? Just look at how many series from last year's lineup were either cancelled or are still waiting to see the light of day.

Of course, getting their own main series would have been amazing and I will never stop believing that they deserve that opportunity. But at the end of the day, I would rather have projects that are happening than just a promise of something that may or may not ever happen.

title_en:
What happens when an AI agent starts representing a customer in a business interaction?

Imagine an agent contacting a company, explaining a customer's needs, resolving an issue and following up without the customer having to manage every step.

I believe this will fundamentally change how businesses approach customer experience. They will need more than intelligent agents. They will need ways to understand, manage and govern interactions between their systems and the growing number of personal AI agents.

This is an important perspective from @maltekosub's keynote. @parloa_ai is building towards this next phase of customer experience.

title: 32× growth in one quarter: From 10K to 320K customers across 100+ countries, with over 100 million messages processed.
title_en:
32× growth in one quarter: From 10K to 320K customers across 100+ countries, with over 100 million messages processed.

We are not building just another personal AI product. Our long-term vision for Teamily AI is to build the central platform of the next-generation Agentic Internet, where AI agents deliver services and perform real work directly, no longer confined to traditional web, desktop, or mobile apps distributed through app stores and search engines. Our recent growth has only strengthened my conviction in this vision.

Agent-as-a-Service (AaaS) will be as accessible as connecting with friends on a social network. Just as Google democratized access to information and services in the web era, Teamily AI aims to democratize access to intelligence and services in the Agentic Internet era, making the right intelligence, people, and services equally accessible to everyone.

In this letter to Teamily AI customers, ecosystem partners, and investors, we share our growth, reflect on our early foresight and what we've built, discuss how we see the evolving AI agent landscape, and outline where we're heading next.

A demo proves an AI agent can work.

Production proves it can work reliably, securely, and at scale.

Here are the 7 essential engineering stages.

𝟭. 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿 | 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺 & 𝗦𝘂𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀
Define the use case, target users, measurable KPIs, and risks (security, privacy, bias).
𝟮. 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 | 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗔𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲
Choose ReAct or Plan-Execute, define decision flows, guardrails, and human approval points.
𝟯. 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁 | 𝗧𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀 & 𝗠𝗲𝗺𝗼𝗿𝘆
Integrate APIs, manage context and memory, and enforce least-privilege tool access.

𝟰. 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘁 | 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀
Build structured prompts, function schemas, few-shot examples, and output constraints.
𝟱. 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 | 𝗥𝗔𝗚 & 𝗞𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲
Prepare and chunk data, implement keyword/vector retrieval, and enforce source permissions.
𝟲. 𝗧𝗲𝘀𝘁 | 𝗘𝘃𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆

• No clear KPIs → No way to measure value.

• 不可观察性→ 事件恢复困难。

title:
A claim can survive for decades. Evidence cannot.

That is what stayed with me reading about Britain’s 2013 settlement w
title_en:
A claim can survive for decades. Evidence cannot.

That is what stayed with me reading about Britain’s 2013 settlement with 5,228 Kenyan claimants over torture and ill-treatment during the colonial Emergency.

The abuses dated back to 1952–1963. By the time the settlement arrived, more than half a century separated the harm from the remedy.

That gap changes more than the calendar.

Witnesses disappear. Records become harder to find. Memory weakens. Delay can start deciding what can still be proved before anyone decides what was right.

That is the justice problem I keep thinking about as AI agents begin making deals at machine speed.

Speed is not just convenience here.

It helps preserve the dispute while the facts are still fresh.

Speed is not just convenience here.

一项索赔可以持续数十年。证据不能。

title:
The public internet will not survive the AI revolution.

My best guess as to what replaces it is AI to AI communication
title_en:
The public internet will not survive the AI revolution.

My best guess as to what replaces it is AI to AI communication protocols and relationship graphs built on how well the AI understands you.

Most SaaS apps will die and what remains will end up as ephemeral modules - a subset of what the intelligence working for you occasionally develops, maintains and uses on your behalf to assist in achieving your true goals. 

Every individual and business will have their own AI Agent that represents them.

You can think of this like an 'Agent in a Box' - you will get AI voice, video, text, images; literally all modalities so cheap it's basically free.

For businesses, most will end up using open weight AI models for these agents in a box, since they won't want their proprietary data leaking to the frontier model providers, and will want to control the 'learning loop' derived from their verified business history, payments and customer and interactions.

Now this is where it gets interesting.

I think most businesses will use open weight models for agents in a box, but then these agents will post to a decentralised, common, privacy-preserving protocol that stores verifiable facts about that business and their operations.

You can think of this as the modern day AI equivalent of what Google My Business currently is.

Once that stuff goes on-chain, guess what?

Now when users ask their AI to 'find me a mechanic near me' it checks the protocol for the best match based on data that cannot be faked - real payments data, for example, and real reviews from biometrically signed humans.

In this way, almost all interactions start with the AI, get mediated between other AIs, and help match user intent based on the on-chain, privacy-preserved data.

Since each AI will also have a very deep knowledge graph of who everyone is (it will have all your data and you will talk to it all the time), they will be able to use this same protocol for all types of matching services and escrow, basically eliminating the old web 2.0 two sided marketplaces entirely.

All sorts of other use cases open up once this stuff becomes available, like clearing houses for agents, pooled aggregate demand for group buying, representative democracy that is actually representiative, insurance, auditing, etc because all interactions involving actual business interactions will be transparent, but private and verifiable.

And that is how the new AI-first 'internet' is born. 

Websites, SaaS apps, all that other crap, gets subsumed by the intelligence and generated on the fly.

Intelligence is all that matters in the end, it is a black hole.

full_text_zh:
公共互联网将无法在人工智能革命中幸存下来。

我对替代它的最好猜测是人工智能对人工智能的通信协议和基于人工智能对你的理解程度而建立的关系图。

大多数 SaaS 应用程序都会消亡，剩下的将最终成为临时模块——为您工作的情报的一个子集，偶尔会代表您开发、维护和使用，以帮助您实现真正的目标。

每个个人和企业都会有自己的人工智能代理来代表他们。

你可以把它想象成一个“盒子里的代理”——你将获得人工智能语音、视频、文本、图像；几乎所有的方式都很便宜，基本上都是免费的。

对于企业来说，大多数人最终都会为这些代理使用开放式权重人工智能模型，因为他们不希望自己的专有数据泄露给前沿模型提供商，并且希望控制从其经过验证的业务历史、支付、客户和交互中得出的“学习循环”。

现在这就是有趣的地方。

我认为，大多数企业将为盒子中的代理使用开放权重模型，但这些代理将发布到一个分散的、通用的、保护隐私的协议，该协议存储有关该企业及其运营的可验证事实。

您可以将其视为现代人工智能，相当于目前的“Google 我的商家”。

一旦这些东西上链，你猜怎么着？

现在，当用户要求他们的人工智能“找到我附近的机械师”时，它会根据无法伪造的数据（例如真实的支付数据，以及来自生物识别签名的人类的真实评论）检查协议是否有最佳匹配。

通过这种方式，几乎所有交互都从人工智能开始，在其他人工智能之间进行调解，并根据链上、隐私保护的数据帮助匹配用户意图。

由于每个人工智能还将拥有一个非常深入的知识图谱，了解每个人是谁（它将拥有您的所有数据，并且您将一直与它交谈），因此他们将能够对所有类型的匹配服务和托管使用相同的协议，基本上完全消除旧的 Web 2.0 双边市场。

一旦这些东西可用，各种其他用例就会开放，比如代理商的清算所、团购的汇集总需求、实际上具有代表性的代议制民主、保险、审计等，因为涉及实际业务交互的所有交互都将是透明的，但私密且可验证。

这就是新的人工智能优先的“互联网”的诞生。

网站、SaaS 应用程序以及所有其他垃圾，都被智能所包含并动态生成。

智力最终才是最重要的，它是一个黑洞。

title_en:
$ICP Q3 2026 Recap

🔹 $ICP gained 58.9% in Q3, from $2.10 to $3.33. It bottomed near $2.02 at the start of August, then ran 38.9% in September alone.

AI and developer tools

🔹 ICP MCP Preview: DFINITY released an MCP server that lets AI assistants find $ICP apps, read the data canisters expose and, once the user approves, take actions inside those apps.

🔹 Caffeine Milestone: DFINITY founder Dominic Williams said Caffeine has now generated more than 15 billion lines of code.

🔹 Moxzi Alpha: Developers shipped the first public alpha of Moxzi, a Motoko compiler written in Motoko. You can build locally, in a browser tab or remotely through an $ICP canister, with no OCaml toolchain.

Sovereign cloud

🔹 Cloud Engines Dashboard: The ICP Dashboard now has its own Cloud Engines view. It shows engine counts, data centers, node providers and machine classes separately from mainnet.

🔹 UNDP x DFINITY: The UN Development Programme and DFINITY partnered to test sovereign cloud and decentralized AI in public services. Pilots run through UNDP country offices, civil society groups and government programs, using Cloud Engines and Caffeine.

SNS launches

🔹 Menese Protocol: Menese announced plans to decentralize through an $ICP SNS, aiming to raise 100,000 to 500,000 ICP for listings, infrastructure and cross-chain liquidity.

🔹 Doxa: Doxa’s SNS swap went live with a 50,000 $ICP minimum to fund DoxaUSD, its stablecoin project on ICP.

$ICP Q3 2026 Recap

🔹 $ICP gained 58.9% in Q3, from $2.10 to $3.33. It bottomed near $2.02 at the start of August, then ran 38.9% in September alone.

AI and developer tools

🔹 ICP MCP Preview: DFINITY released an MCP server that lets AI assistants find $ICP apps, read the data canisters expose and, once the user approves, take actions inside those apps.

SNS launches

title:
an AI agent should have rules before it gets access to capital

giving an AI agent access to funds without defining its
title_en:
an AI agent should have rules before it gets access to capital

giving an AI agent access to funds without defining its limits is not automation i would be comfortable with 

markets move quickly, opportunities change, and even a well designed strategy can experience unexpected losses

this is why the permission structure behind @meetmotes deserves attention

users can establish rules around how their agents operate 

think about practical controls such as:

maximum trade size
daily spending limits
acceptable slippage
stop loss conditions
approved assets and strategies

these boundaries help separate useful automation from unrestricted financial control 

the interesting part is that the agent can still analyze opportunities and make decisions within the mandate provided by its owner 

for me, that is a more sensible direction for AI powered finance

the goal should not be to remove humans from every decision

it should be to give them better tools while keeping meaningful control in their hands

title: Before Carl Menger published his Principles of Economics in 1871, mainstream economic thought was a muddle of half-truth
title_en:
Before Carl Menger published his Principles of Economics in 1871, mainstream economic thought was a muddle of half-truths, moral philosophy dressed as science, and a value theory so broken it could not explain why water costs less than diamonds.

The classical school, anchored by Adam Smith and David Ricardo, gave the world the labor theory of value. Price, they believed, derived from the labor embedded in production. Ricardo built elaborate theoretical structures on this foundation. Karl Marx then took the same foundation and built a guillotine with it. The logic was internally consistent and empirically catastrophic.

Classical economists could not explain prices consumers actually paid. A painting by Raphael required fewer labor hours than a competently built brick wall, yet sold for vastly more. They patched this with awkward exceptions and caveats, which is what economists do when the theory contradicts reality but they refuse to abandon the theory(As Keynesians still do today).

John Stuart Mill represents the peak of this confusion. His 1848 Principles of Political Economy ran through five editions and taught a generation of British policymakers that price emerged from supply and production costs, with demand treated as almost an afterthought.

Meanwhile, Say's Law told economists that production creates its own demand. This carried a grain of truth and a mountain of overconfidence. Nobody had yet placed the individual decision-maker, weighing one marginal unit against the next, at the center of economic analysis until Carl Menger came along. 

Shockingly, 150 years later, serious people in serious positions still refuse to believe subjective value theory and the theory of marginal utility. They still think and act as if value is derived from labor.

full_text_en:
Before Carl Menger published his Principles of Economics in 1871, mainstream economic thought was a muddle of half-truths, moral philosophy dressed as science, and a value theory so broken it could not explain why water costs less than diamonds.

The classical school, anchored by Adam Smith and David Ricardo, gave the world the labor theory of value. Price, they believed, derived from the labor embedded in production. Ricardo built elaborate theoretical structures on this foundation. Karl Marx then took the same foundation and built a guillotine with it. The logic was internally consistent and empirically catastrophic.

Classical economists could not explain prices consumers actually paid. A painting by Raphael required fewer labor hours than a competently built brick wall, yet sold for vastly more. They patched this with awkward exceptions and caveats, which is what economists do when the theory contradicts reality but they refuse to abandon the theory(As Keynesians still do today).

John Stuart Mill represents the peak of this confusion. His 1848 Principles of Political Economy ran through five editions and taught a generation of British policymakers that price emerged from supply and production costs, with demand treated as almost an afterthought.

Meanwhile, Say's Law told economists that production creates its own demand. This carried a grain of truth and a mountain of overconfidence. Nobody had yet placed the individual decision-maker, weighing one marginal unit against the next, at the center of economic analysis until Carl Menger came along. 

Shockingly, 150 years later, serious people in serious positions still refuse to believe subjective value theory and the theory of marginal utility. They still think and act as if value is derived from labor.
full_text_zh:
在卡尔·门格尔于 1871 年发表《经济学原理》之前，主流经济思想是半真半假、披着科学外衣的道德哲学和价值理论的混乱，以至于无法解释为什么水的价格比钻石便宜。

以亚当·斯密和大卫·李嘉图为代表的古典学派为世界带来了劳动价值论。他们认为，价格源自生产中的劳动力。李嘉图在此基础上建立了详尽的理论结构。卡尔·马克思随后采用了同样的基础并用它建造了一座断头台。这个逻辑在内部是一致的，但从经验来看却是灾难性的。

古典经济学家无法解释消费者实际支付的价格。拉斐尔的一幅画所需的工时比建造一堵合格的砖墙要少，但售价却高得多。他们用令人尴尬的例外和警告来弥补这一点，这就是经济学家在理论与现实相矛盾时所做的事情，但他们拒绝放弃该理论（就像凯恩斯主义者今天仍然这样做的那样）。

约翰·斯图尔特·密尔代表了这种混乱的顶峰。他于 1848 年出版的《政治经济学原理》共出版了五个版本，并教导一代英国政策制定者：价格源于供给和生产成本，而需求几乎被视为事后的想法。

与此同时，萨伊定律告诉经济学家，生产创造自己的需求。这话有一定道理，但也充满了过度自信。在卡尔·门格尔出现之前，还没有人将衡量一个边际单位与另一个边际单位的个人决策者置于经济分析的中心。

令人震惊的是，150年后，严肃的人仍然拒绝相信主观价值理论和边际效用理论。他们的思维和行为仍然认为价值是从劳动中获得的。

title: An AI agent doesn't have to know how to do everything. It just needs a way to find help when a task goes beyond its capa
title_en:
An AI agent doesn't have to know how to do everything. It just needs a way to find help when a task goes beyond its capabilities.

That’s an interesting idea behind the Agents Helping Agents Bounty feature on https://t.co/wITmf7ceVM by @termix_ai.

Here’s how it works:

Imagine an agent receives a job but cannot complete one part of it independently. Instead of abandoning the entire task, it can create a bounty on https://t.co/BOxbHxlLgM and invite other specialized agents to contribute.

The process opens up a collaborative workflow:

• Post a bounty: The agent publishes the task it needs help completing.

• Attract specialists: Other agents can discover the bounty and take on the work.

• Complete the task: Participating agents deliver their assigned results.

• Verify the output: The submitted work goes through verification.

• Earn the reward: Agents whose contributions pass verification receive the agreed reward.

Why does this matter?

Because it changes how we think about autonomous agents.

Instead of expecting one agent to handle every problem, agents can become coordinators that delegate specialized work to others.

A research agent can request help with data analysis. A development agent can outsource design. A larger project can be divided into smaller tasks handled by different specialists.

This is how an agent economy becomes collaborative rather than competitive alone.

With @termix_ai, the bigger opportunity is not just agents completing jobs, but agents creating opportunities for other agents to earn by contributing their capabilities.

One agent's limitation can become another agent's opportunity.

full_text_zh:
人工智能代理不必知道如何做所有事情。它只是需要一种在任务超出其能力范围时寻求帮助的方法。

这是 @termix_ai 在 上的代理帮助代理赏金功能背后的一个有趣的想法。

它的工作原理如下：

想象一下，一名代理人收到一份工作，但无法独立完成其中的一部分。它可以在 上创建赏金并邀请其他专业代理做出贡献，而不是放弃整个任务。

该过程开启了协作工作流程：

• 发布赏金：代理发布需要帮助完成的任务。

• 吸引专家：其他特工可以发现赏金并承担工作。

• 完成任务：参与代理交付分配给他们的结果。

• 验证输出：提交的工作经过验证。

• 获得奖励：贡献通过验证的代理商将获得约定的奖励。

为什么这很重要？

因为它改变了我们对自主代理的看法。

代理可以成为将专门工作委托给其他人的协调员，而不是期望一个代理能够处理所有问题。

研究代理可以请求数据分析方面的帮助。开发代理可以外包设计。较大的项目可以分为较小的任务，由不同的专家处理。

这就是代理经济变得协作而不是单独竞争的方式。

有了@termix_ai，更大的机会不仅仅是座席完成工作，而是座席为其他座席创造机会，通过贡献自己的能力来赚钱。

一位代理人的限制可能会成为另一位代理人的机会。

title:
Most people think using Claude Code is about writing better prompts.

It’s not.

The real unlock is structuring your rep
title_en:
Most people think using Claude Code is about writing better prompts.

It’s not.

The real unlock is structuring your repository so Claude can think like an engineer.

If your repo is messy, Claude behaves like a chatbot.

If your repo is structured, Claude behaves like a developer living inside your codebase.

Your project only needs 4 things:

• the why → what the system does
• the map → where things live
• the rules → what’s allowed / forbidden
• the workflows → how work gets done

I call this:

The Anatomy of a Claude Code Project 👇

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1️⃣ CLAUDE.md = Repo Memory (Keep it Short)

This file is the north star for Claude.

Not a massive document.

Just three things:

• Purpose → why the system exists
• Repo map → how the project is structured
• Rules + commands → how Claude should operate

If CLAUDE.md becomes too long, the model starts missing critical signals.

Clarity beats size.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2️⃣ .claude/skills/ = Reusable Expert Modes

Stop repeating instructions in prompts.

Turn common workflows into reusable skills.

Examples:

• code review checklist
• refactoring playbook
• debugging workflow
• release procedures

Now Claude can switch into specialized modes instantly.

Result:

More consistent outputs across sessions and teammates.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

3️⃣ .claude/hooks/ = Guardrails

Models forget.

Hooks don’t.

Use hooks for things that must always happen automatically.

Examples:

• run formatters after edits
• trigger tests after core changes
• block sensitive directories (auth, billing, migrations)

Hooks turn AI workflows into reliable engineering systems.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

4️⃣ docs/ = Progressive Context

Don’t overload prompts with information.

Instead, let Claude navigate your documentation.

Examples:

• architecture overview
• ADRs (engineering decisions)
• operational runbooks

Claude doesn’t need everything in memory.

It just needs to know where truth lives.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

5️⃣ Local CLAUDE.md for Critical Modules

Some areas of your system have hidden complexity.

Add local context files there.

Example:

src/auth/CLAUDE.md
src/persistence/CLAUDE.md
infra/CLAUDE.md

Now Claude understands the danger zones exactly when it works in them.

This dramatically reduces mistakes.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Here’s the shift most people miss:

Prompting is temporary.

Structure is permanent.

Once your repository is designed for AI:

Claude stops acting like a chatbot...

…and starts behaving like a project-native engineer. 🚀

Follow @swadeshkumar_ for more !!
